title: Cold rebuild: A gateway in front
summary: Rebuild A gateway in front from memory, no hints.

steps.title: Cold rebuild
body: Time to prove a piece stuck. You built **A gateway in front** in *Gateway, integration, backend: what goes where*. Now write it again from an
**empty editor**: no starter, no hints, no solution to peek at. The tests are exactly the ones you passed
Why: pulling something out of memory is what makes it stay there. Reading your old code feels like knowing
it; rebuilding it cold shows whether you do. If you get stuck, that is useful news: go back to the lesson,
then come back and try again tomorrow.
This check, plus the boss, is what proves the module.

code: Func<string?, int> backend = token => { calls++; return 200; };
Func<string?, int> gateway = token => token == "good" ? backend(token) : 401;
steps.explain: Rejected calls stop at the gateway. That protects every system behind it from load and from unauthenticated traffic.

steps.title: Rebuild A gateway in front cold
prompt: The tests declare these types (you don't write them):
record Req(string Path, Dictionary<string, string> Headers);
Write `Handler Gateway(Handler next, HashSet<string> validTokens)` that returns a handler which:
- answers `new Res(401, "unauthorized")` when there is no `Authorization` header, it does not start with `Bearer `, or the token after it is not in `validTokens`;

- otherwise calls `next` with a **new** `Req`: same path, a **copy** of the headers **without** `Authorization` (the consumer's token must not reach the backend). Don't change the caller's dictionary.
Header names are case-insensitive: build the copy with `StringComparer.OrdinalIgnoreCase`.
**From memory this time:** the editor starts empty and the tests are the ones you passed in the lesson.
